mc: The ocean fragment shader does not compile because it reads p.z from a vec2. The console shows shader errors and the ocean never draws, so the space beyond the rocks is empty sky.
The polar limit keeps the camera above the ground, but the max distance lets it pull back past the terrain edge. From there the headland reads as a flat slab floating in empty sky.
The load is moderate, one shadow map, one terrain mesh, procedural sky and simple primitives. A standard laptop should hold 30 fps.
No UI, no text and no buttons. Orbit is the only interaction.
Clouds drift, the grass sways, snow drifts and the lens turns as soon as the page loads.
The horizon sits higher than in the photo and the tower is smaller in frame. The rock outcrops that fill the photo’s foreground are replaced by a snow slope.
White octagonal tapered tower, red lantern and cap, white gallery rail. The colours and silhouette read as the photo, though the model adds a small gabled porch that the photo doesn’t have.
The shore reads as a smooth snow field. The boulders render dark red and magenta because their vertex colour data gets multiplied into the rock colour, so it doesn’t read as a snowy granite shore.
The ocean shader fails to compile, so no sea is visible beyond the rocks.
Clear blue gradient sky with a pale horizon and low sun from the left, as in the photo.
Slender tapered octagonal shaft with the lantern on top, close to the photo’s proportions.
The lantern has glazed panes with red mullions and a white railing gallery around it.
The boulders are noise-displaced spheres with a faceted low-poly look and no real cracks. The crack lines on the terrain are only painted on.
The right whaleback bump is added after the plinth pad is flattened, so the ground rises up to about 0.4 m around the base and buries it unevenly. One boulder also overlaps the tower base.
There is no ocean, so orbiting shows the edge of the terrain slab against empty sky.
One directional sun with a shadow map, and all shadows fall to the right.
The tower shows a lit left face and a cool grey shaded side, and it is not blown out.
The sky has a haze band, but with the sea missing there is no sea horizon fading into it. The distant coast reads as a flat grey slab.
No area is fully black or clipped to white. The darkest parts are the red boulders in shadow.
Pure white flat shaded paint with no grime, streaks or wear. It reads as clean plastic.
The snow is plausible, but the rock reads as glossy red plastic and there is no darker wet rock at the waterline.
The glass is a 38% opacity pane with no environment map, so it is see-through but reflects no sky.
The ocean is not drawn. Even in the shader code, the water colour comes only from noise, with no shift by depth.
The horizon is level and the camera has no roll.
The ocean doesn’t render, so no waves are visible.
There is no visible sea and no spray system at all, so nothing breaks on the rocks.
The foam lives inside the ocean shader that fails to compile, so no foam shows.
Snow drifts across the rock from left to right and the grass tufts sway in the wind.
Motion runs on a real time clock at believable speeds, and the drifting snow wraps with a fade, so nothing jumps.
The ocean is missing, so this can’t be judged as a pass.
There are no spray particles in the scene. The only particles are small snow points.
No water is drawn, so the terrain edge drops into empty sky instead of meeting the sea with foam.
Red boulders, the missing ocean and the plain snow foreground make the paused frame read clearly as CG, not as the photo.
